hook: Shaoqing Ren earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Science and Technology of China in 2011 and then entered a joint PhD program between USTC and Microsoft Research Asia under the supervision of Jian Sun. During that period he co-authored Faster R-CNN in 2015, which merged region proposal generation directly into a convolutional network to make object detection dramatically faster, and Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition in 2016, which introduced the residual connections that made it practical to train networks hundreds of layers deep. In September 2016 he co-founded the autonomous driving startup Momenta, which reached unicorn valuation within three years. He became Senior Vice President of Autonomous Driving at NIO in August 2020. In September 2025 he returned to USTC as an Endowed Chair Professor leading its Artificial General Intelligence Institute.
name: Shaoqing Ren

quote.text: We further merge RPN and Fast R-CNN into a single network by sharing their convolutional features.
quote.context: From the abstract of the 2015 paper "Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks," co-authored with Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, and Jian Sun.

moniker: Co-creator of ResNet and Faster R-CNN

primary.name: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks (arXiv, 2015)

timeline.event: Received a BEng from the University of Science and Technology of China.
timeline.impact: Set the stage for his joint doctoral research with Microsoft Research Asia.

timeline.event: Co-authored "Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks" with Kaiming He, Ross Girshick, and Jian Sun.
timeline.impact: Made real-time, learned object detection practical by folding region proposals into the detection network itself.

timeline.event: Co-authored "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition" with Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, and Jian Sun.
timeline.impact: Introduced residual connections that solved the degradation problem in very deep networks and won the CVPR 2016 Best Paper Award.

timeline.event: Co-founded the autonomous driving startup Momenta.
timeline.impact: Applied his computer vision research to self-driving perception systems at commercial scale.

timeline.event: Became Senior Vice President of Autonomous Driving at NIO.
timeline.impact: Took on leadership of self-driving technology development at a major electric vehicle manufacturer.

timeline.event: Received the Future Science Prize in Mathematics and Computer Science.
timeline.impact: Recognized the lasting research impact of ResNet and Faster R-CNN.

timeline.event: Joined USTC as an Endowed Chair Professor leading its Artificial General Intelligence Institute.
timeline.impact: Returned to academia to pursue longer-horizon research after nearly a decade in industry.

quick_facts: BEng from the University of Science and Technology of China, 2011
PhD through a joint USTC and Microsoft Research Asia program, advised by Jian Sun
Co-authored both ResNet and Faster R-CNN
Co-founded the autonomous driving company Momenta in 2016
Served as Senior Vice President of Autonomous Driving at NIO from 2020
Received the Future Science Prize in Mathematics and Computer Science, 2023

achievements.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (2016)
achievements.impact: Co-authored the ResNet paper, which introduced residual connections that made it possible to train neural networks hundreds of layers deep and became a foundation of modern computer vision.

achievements.title: Faster R-CNN (2015)
achievements.impact: Unified region proposal generation and object classification into one network, making accurate object detection fast enough for practical use and shaping later detection systems.

achievements.title: Co-founder of Momenta (2016)
achievements.impact: Helped build an autonomous driving software company that reached unicorn status within three years of founding.

achievements.title: Future Science Prize in Mathematics and Computer Science (2023)
achievements.impact: Recognized his contributions to computer vision research underlying modern object detection and recognition systems.
